auth_type.correction: oauth2; requests use a Bearer access token, obtained either as a personal access token for the user's own data or through an OAuth client for third-party apps

rate_limits.correction: No numeric HTTP request quota is stated, but Tibber publishes a maximum of two open WebSockets and requires backoff; it also recommends querying today/tomorrow prices only once daily.

example.correction: curl -X POST https://api.tibber.com/v1-beta/gql -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "User-Agent: MyApp/1.0.0" -d '{"query":"{ viewer { name homes { id address { address1 city } } } }"}'

description.correction: The GraphQL API exposes prices, consumption, production, home metadata, and Pulse/Watty live measurements. Its current schema does not expose operations for controlling EV chargers or smart plugs; Tibber's separate Data API handles device identity, state, and history.

notes: The API remains documented and operational, but the entry conflates Tibber's older GraphQL API with its separate device-focused Data API. It also misclassifies Bearer access-token authentication, invents device-control capability, omits a required User-Agent header, and overlooks published WebSocket/backoff limits. Official sources do not establish a standalone free pricing tier.
